name: M. Chapoutier Crozes-Ermitage Les Varonniers 2015
text:
## M. Chapoutier Crozes-Ermitage Les Varonniers 2015

**The story.** Maison M. Chapoutier, based at [Tain-l'Hermitage](https://www.google.com/maps?q=M.+Chapoutier,+Tain-l'Hermitage,+France&t=k), traces its roots in the Rhône to 1808; Polydor Chapoutier bought the first vineyards in 1879. Max Chapoutier ran it until 1977, when his sons Michel and Marc took over, and under Michel the wines improved through the 1980s and won international recognition by the end of the decade ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier)). All its vineyards are farmed [biodynamically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture), which Chapoutier says has been at the heart of its philosophy since 1991 ([Chapoutier](https://www.chapoutier.com/en/shop/les-varonniers/2015/152)), and it prefers single-variety wines even where blends are common.

**The wine: Les Varonniers.** Les Varonniers is Chapoutier's top [Crozes-Hermitage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crozes-Hermitage_AOC) (Chapoutier spells it "Ermitage"), from its oldest vines there, over 60 years old on average. They grow on south-east-facing granite slopes at the end of the Hermitage hill and on river terraces at the "Chassis" plot. It is 100% [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), hand-harvested, fermented for about a month in small concrete tanks, using only free-run juice, and aged 14 to 18 months in oak casks, some new. Chapoutier says that, depending on the vintage, it can keep 30 to 60 years, even 50 to 75 ([Chapoutier](https://www.chapoutier.com/en/shop/les-varonniers/2015/152)).

**About Crozes-Hermitage.** Crozes-Hermitage is the largest appellation in the northern Rhône, about half the region's vineyards, and is usually less highly regarded than its famous neighbour [Hermitage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitage_AOC); a panel of tasters already praised its likeness to Hermitage in 1846. It became an appellation in 1937 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crozes-Hermitage_AOC)). Les Varonniers shows what its best old vines can do.

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-rhone) says 2015 was "universally viewed as a vintage with top quality potential", though overshadowed by the even better 2016 and 2017. With such ripe fruit, keeping freshness and avoiding over-extraction was the key to quality.

**What the critics say for 2015.** As listed by [Chapoutier](https://www.chapoutier.com/en/shop/les-varonniers/2015/152):
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 93**. Full-bodied and rich, "already almost enjoyable to drink", with bold layers of cassis, mulberries and spice; close to jammy but held back by "a delicious savory edge of black olive on the velvety finish".
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 93**. Opaque ruby: powerful, mineral blackberry, licorice, flowers and olive paste; velvety, broad and concentrated, with black and blue fruit liqueur, cola and candied violet, and a strikingly long, smoky finish.
- **La Revue du Vin de France: 15.5/20**.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.0** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (Chapoutier's page also lists a Jeb Dunnuck score without his note, so I've left it out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2023 to 2030, though Chapoutier says it can keep for decades. So it is in its drinking window now: blackcurrant, raspberry, licorice, graphite and granite minerality. Decant an hour ahead.

**Serving and food.** Chapoutier suggests all meats and poultry, charcuterie and cheeses. My picks: grilled lamb chops, beef with a pepper sauce, or duck.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Les Varonniers at the moment; look to fine-wine merchants.

**Curious details**
- **Braille on every label.** Since 1996, every Chapoutier label has included Braille ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier)).
- **Free-run only.** Les Varonniers uses only free-run juice, none of the harder pressed wine ([Chapoutier](https://www.chapoutier.com/en/shop/les-varonniers/2015/152)).
